This research investigates the effects of class imbalance on three distinct machine learning techniques - two traditional algorithms (k-nearest neighbors and support vector machines) and a more contemporary method (neural networks). The method under consideration employs a simple, non-parametric proxy model to mitigate class imbalance issues within the training process. Experimental results reveal that class imbalance significantly impairs performance in both the k-nearest neighbors and support vector machines methods, but exhibits a more nuanced response in neural networks.

Our research explores the COVID-19 coverage in US local news across varying regions and political landscapes by measuring news volume, frame, and microtext on the microblogging platform, Medium. By examining 640 local news sources in 400 metropolitan areas from July 2020 to January 2021, our study aimed to understand the impact of geography and politics on local COVID-19 coverage. The research found that local news volume expanded in early 2020, declining later, with content influenced by people, place, and microtext, while also showing people-related frames dominating volume and political source frames correlating with local news volume. The study's findings are of particular interest to policymakers, journalists, and researchers, as they contribute to a better understanding of local COVID-19 coverage patterns.

A specialized application of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) has been tailored to improve the computational efficiency of tree codes in astrophysical simulations. This modified FBM method optimizes the calculation of particle interactions by taking into account their unique properties, particularly when confined to flat, periodic, or gravity-dominated environments. By adapting the method to these distinct scenarios, it significantly accelerates certain particle interactions. Moreover, when integrated into a tree code, the optimized BDTree method yields a notable performance improvement over traditional methods. Our analysis demonstrates that this is based on the careful selection of the cell size to kernel radius ratio, ensuring both accuracy and computational efficiency. Our implementation in a three-dimensional tree code framework effectively combines the efficiency of the BDTree method with that of multi-level methods, resulting in significant performance gains.

The electron-proton collision process, where the proton is left intact and high-energy photons are produced at very low angles with a proton in the final stage, is studied with a focus on its double spin asymmetry. This asymmetry is measured and found to be consistent with the current theoretical framework of the Soffer relation. Experimental results are collected based on data collected from a total of 2.4 inverse femtobarns. In these experiments, photon and proton detection is carried out at distinct angular positions and double spin asymmetry measurements are reported. A critical evaluation of the measurements and associated uncertainties is also presented.

Behavior cloning, a powerful RL method, faces limitations in handling student policy discrepancies with the expert data. Recent advances in augmented realities have shown promising results in improving performance through efficient use of time-efficient expert labels. We explore how policy cloning is applied in high-dimensional control problems, focusing on efficient policy learning from time-efficient expert labels. Our emphasis lies in leveraging these augmentations to bridge the gap between expert behavior and student policy. We have developed two types of augmentations, which enable effective behavior imitation by correctly identifying expert actions, despite a student policy falling short with the expert data. We demonstrate the benefits of our approach on challenging control tasks, providing both qualitative and quantitative results.

A novel search method for newly formed, resonance-like particles ($A$) in colliding high-energy protons at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has been introduced. This approach focuses on the rare decay of $A$ into a standard model neutral particle ($h$) and a $Z$ particle, where $Z$ decays into a pair of charged leptons. The standard model neutral particle ($h$) then decays into a pair of tau particles. By utilizing data collected at a high integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb$^{-1}$ from 13 TeV proton-proton collisions at the CMS experiment, the search specifically targets cases in which the mass of the new particle ($A$) lies between 500 and 1500 GeV and its mass as a standard model neutral scalar particle ($h$) lies between 120 and 130 GeV. No unusual patterns were found in the data, and the search's statistical limits on new particle formation have been translated into limits on a particular type of theoretical model that involves extended standard models.

In the context of resonant spin maser systems, particularly those based on the research of Cook et al. (2015) utilizing 20122012 nuclear magnetic spin ensembles, digital signal processing and adaptive control methods have been incorporated to further refine the stability and optimal performance of the system. An automated mass production method for highly pure 20122012 cubic crystals was implemented, containing more than $10^{14}$ uniform spin ensembles, which served as the resonant cavities in the study. By employing digital signal processing and adaptive control, the research achieved a notable breakthrough in stabilizing the frequency of the nuclear magnetic resonance, thereby decreasing its standard deviation by more than one order of magnitude. Furthermore, optical detection of magnetic resonance frequencies has been successfully modified to allow for real-time monitoring and adjustment of maser frequencies, resulting in increased efficiency and reduced variability. With the addition of digital processing, the system exhibited longer continuous frequencies, lasting around 20 seconds, along with decreased frequency deviations of less than 10 Hz and decreased initial and steady-state off-center frequencies of around $10^{-4}$ Hz. These improvements highlight the significant advancements possible through the integration of digital processing in quantum maser systems.

Recent breakthroughs in the study of hypergeometric groups have allowed for significant progress in understanding K3 surface automorphisms. In this study, we build on this progress by examining the hyperbolic fixed points of hyperbolic hypergeometric groups, in addition to the already established elliptic and loxodromic cases. To achieve this, we establish novel identities for hypergeometric elliptic integrals, incorporating both the singular values of the absolute elliptic curve and non-singular periods, using insights from the underlying Picard-Lefschetz theory.

This research investigates the capability of the future International Linear Collider to identify two hidden states: a neutral particle from the visible sector ($\chi_{\scriptsize V}$) decaying into a lower-energy neutral particle from the hidden sector ($\chi_{\scriptsize h}$) and a high-energy gamma ray, as well as a massive, long-lived particle that escapes detection. Both scenarios occur within the framework of a scaled version of the minimal supersymmetric standard model that also incorporates a five-dimensional warping mechanism, featuring the spontaneous breaking of a $U(1)$ gauge symmetry between sectors through the interaction of neutralinos in both sectors. The researchers analyze visible sector neutralinos with masses below 200 GeV that interact with a much lighter hidden sector neutralino and a mesoscopic lifetime in the range $10^{-6}$-$10^{2}$ seconds, and hidden sector neutralinos with a non-zero coupling to a longer-lived messenger neutralino with a range of masses 5-200 GeV. The study examines the effectiveness of the ILC to detect these signatures, taking into account a reduced set of background events, with results for the observation of these phenomena with 1 ab$^{-1}$ of data collection.

We propose a method to assign quantum numbers to simple graphs using graph homology, allowing for further analysis through quantum deformation. This approach incorporates both the graph's topological properties, such as its genus, which determines how it can be placed on surfaces, and its algebraic characteristics, such as the number of maximal edges, also known as the graph clique number. In our formulation, the graphs' quantum numbers are represented by two q-deformed polynomials that are generated from the graph's matching chain complex and its ideal of matching polynomials. These q-deformed quantities, $\bar{q}[2g-2]$ and $q-\binom{n}{\nu}$, respectively, relate to the graph's genus and clique number.

This study introduces an innovative variation of the coordinate ascent method, specifically the block coordinate ascent method, which processes multiple coordinates simultaneously in each iteration. However, in practical applications, simultaneously updating coordinates often requires substantial communication resources and time, posing significant challenges. To overcome this issue, we develop a communication-efficient Block KASCO method that utilizes all available coordinates without requiring simultaneous updates, thereby optimizing communication effects. Our approach incorporates Nearest Neighbor Probability (NNP) within each block to enhance Nefedov's probability, thereby encouraging updates to optimize communications, and employs an optimized step size for improved convergence. We prove the method's feasibility and convergence under general convex objectives, and simultaneously demonstrate its accelerating convergence under strictly convex objectives. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed method over existing approaches, including Block KASCO without optimization and traditional KASCO.

Transfer learning allows models to efficiently train languages by leveraging their common historical roots, thereby accelerating the process. The method involves pre-training on the source language, typically written in the Latin script, and then fine-tuning it on the target language, which often belongs to the same linguistic family but may have been influenced by other scripts. We investigate the transfer of language from Latin to other Central European languages, which are all part of the Slavic and Romance language families. We compare the efficiency of training on the smaller Czech language versus the larger English language and find that training on English leads to better outcomes when translating to Polish. We also investigate the potential of cross-lingual transfer between English and Czech.

The research introduces novel variables to enhance differentiation between electronic and nuclear particle interactions in Gas Time Projection Chamber (GTPCh) data. These novel variables, along with the traditional Landau distribution ratio, are found to significantly outperform the latter when utilized in conjunction with it. The proposed new observables have been tested on a subset of the XENONMT dataset and exhibit improved performance after being incorporated into the existing data dataset. Furthermore, a detailed description of the novel variables and their potential application in next-generation low-mass GTPCh experiments is presented.

This study presents a novel approach to evaluating external driver behavior by assessing environmental factors based on real-time visual observations from the vehicle. Building upon weakly-supervised learning, we utilize brief episodes of expert input and continuous environmental monitoring to establish a behavior model. By combining these elements, we develop a probabilistic framework and a self-supervised learning method for assessing external driver behavior. An evaluation on the CARLA simulator demonstrates that our approach surpasses existing methods under diverse external conditions, paving the way for truly autonomous vehicles.

This study suggests an approach to enhance the OOV generalization of scene text recognition models. A "dictionary-free" OOV model is created by augmenting the OUV with novel synthetic texts generated via GAN-based methods, mimicking the style of the original dataset and tailored to the letter distribution of the OUV. Our model's OOV accuracy is significantly improved, with state-of-the-art results on OUV datasets. The novel OUV-based model achieves a significant boost in accuracy over state-of-the-art models incorporating RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, and Transformers+RNNs. Furthermore, integration of our method with existing models yields substantial enhancements, with models detecting nearly double the amount of novel text during testing compared to models lacking it.

The Kozak-Popescu-Verstraete family of random fields, first described in 2009, captures the dynamics of a quantum spin chain near a quantum phase transition, occurring at a regime boundary between two distinct behaviors. Given the inherent properties of the random field as a function of time-based parameters only, its mathematical representation as a Gaussian process is readily attainable. The underlying covariance kernel's expression, rooted in Bessel function calculations, was initially formulated in terms of hypergeometric expressions. Our recent investigation, based on the series-expansion expression within specific regimes and employing the aid of the fast Fourier transform, enabled calculations of the quantitative similarity between two random fields across various regime combinations.

Recent studies have highlighted the effectiveness of magnetic levitation in manipulating droplets on free surfaces. The key to this method lies in the competition between magnetic energy and surface tension. The induced magnetic deformation of a susceptive liquid enables the application of magnetic torque, thus allowing magnetic levitation. In this work, we examine how a magnetically levitated droplet on a free surface behaves under the influence of an oscillating magnetic field. We find that the initial distortion of the droplet is significantly influenced by this movement, which we can control by adjusting the frequency and amplitude of the magnetic field. Furthermore, we use numerical simulations to confirm this effect and perform stability analysis on the droplet's behavior during its levitation and magnetic manipulation, revealing the complex interplay between the droplet's modes and the parameters at play.

We demonstrate that the Hecke L-functions of primitive SL2(Z) primitive forms exhibit a distinct pattern when compared to those of Spn(Z) cuspidal Hecke eigenforms. For Spn(Z) cuspidal forms, the Sato-Tate theorem's generalized counterparts suggest a specific structure of Hecke eigenvalues as large values, which we then contrast with the observed pattern of Hecke eigenvalues of SL2(Z) primitive forms. By using the adelic language, we provide a unified approach to generalizing Chebyshev inequalities, the gap theorem, and related concepts originally introduced by Chandee, Granville, and Soundararajan, and more recently by Chandee and Soundararajan. Furthermore, we provide further insights into the distribution of primitive SL2(Z) primitive Hecke eigenvalues as large values, by leveraging two key mathematical tools: the Riemann Hypothesis for Galois extensions, and the Selberg zeta function.

The behavior of current and resistance in conventional materials and graphene near ohmic connections varies significantly due to their distinct electronic properties, particularly their linear versus parabolic band structures. However, there has been a lack of comprehensive and unified theoretical models describing the general case of these systems, especially when considering non-equilibrium conditions and external influences like bias voltages. This study provides a complete description of current and resistance for normal-normal graphene connections under arbitrary levels of imbalance and external electric potentials. The findings reveal that the linear dispersion relationship of graphene leads to unique characteristics in current and resistance that cannot be explained by simply extrapolating the standard Fermi gas model. Furthermore, the theoretical framework developed in this work is validated through comparison with ab initio simulations and experimental measurements.

Weakly nonlinear and monotone operators in Banach lattices exhibit convergent behavior for certain initial values under specific conditions, which also apply to weakly asymptotic values of the trajectories. Norm convergence is guaranteed under certain strict monotone conditions. Theoretical findings are illustrated using specific operator types in ordered Banach spaces.

We address a conjecture from [Y. O. V. Tyshkevich, 1994] regarding pancyclic graphs in cubic ones. Specifically, we demonstrate that to prove the pancyclic nature of cubic graphs with $n$ vertices and m independent vertices, it's sufficient to prove it for pancyclic graphs where $n \leq 4m^2$. This outcome holds considerable value as it confirms the pancyclic conjecture in cubic graphs where $n \leq 8m^2$. Moreover, as a side effect, we show that min-2-cycle covers exist in pancyclic graphs where $n \leq 4m^2$, implying a new result concerning the existence of disjoint cycles in pancyclic graphs, specifically, it's known that $n \leq 12m^2$ min 3-cycles cover exist in such graphs.

We've examined how different flow patterns of the medium surrounding light hadrons influence their rapidity distribution. Our findings reveal that even small variations in the medium's initial state have a significant impact. This is because the medium flow creates a gradient in pressure that affects the evolution of the rapidity distribution. Specifically, we observed that the initial medium profile tends to decelerate the growth of transverse momentum, leading to reduced flow velocity and final rapidity at low values of momentum. To improve our understanding, we employed the BJT model, which considered both the binary number of collisions and the behavior of the medium, to investigate the rapidity distribution of charged hadrons. Our investigation revealed that a medium with a more rapid and efficient transfer of transverse momentum to the participating system results in larger values of final rapidity and better agreement with experimental data. This suggests that the BJT model can serve as a valuable tool for studying the complex interactions that occur in the early stages of heavy-ion collisions.

A new machine learning technique called "SASK" has been developed that efficiently solves complex problems described by partial differential equations. This technique combines elements from kernel-based methods and machine learning algorithms of variational inference type to create a variational approximation of Bayesian neural networks. It incorporates analytical calculations of the partial derivatives of both the loss function and model evidence. As a result, a crucial limitation of earlier neural network methods has been significantly alleviated. This allows for a considerable reduction in training time when dealing high-dimensional problems, Partial Differential Equations, and Bayesian Machine Learning in general. This technique achieves this result without compromising the capabilities of traditional Bayesian Neural Networks. This technique achieves this result in L2 norm and while maintaining quantifiable confidence bounds. This technique achieves this result in forward predictions. This technique achieves this result while also avoiding overconfidence.

We compute the resonance parameters of the H$_2$ molecule in DC electric fields using a M\"{o}ller-Sievers transformation and a Spontaneous-Quantization approach. Our results are compared with those from the Basis-Normalization method and align closely, suggesting consistency. Furthermore, our study indicates that the effects of a DC electric field on hydrogen and water molecules can be neglected in molecular spectroscopy.

We investigate how the Sinkhorn algorithm responds to the Schrödinger problem when no solution exists, employing entropy constraints on the interchangeability of the procedure with product formation and conditional expectations. Our analysis reveals that the algorithm converges towards an equilibrium distribution that minimizes the cross-entropy with the prior, even in the absence of a valid solution to the Schrödinger problem.

Measurements of the cross-section for top-quark pair creation are obtained from proton-proton interactions. For the 2015 period, using 37 inverse femtobarns of data, the total cross-section was found to be 151.3 ± 1.5 (statistical) ± 10.0 (systematic) pb, while for the full 2016 dataset, it was found to be 151.2 ± 1.1 (statistical) ± 9.9 (systematic) pb. When considering the experimental uncertainties alone, the cross-section measurements are within one standard deviation of the predictions, but including theoretical uncertainties brings the measurements within two standard deviations. Furthermore, the differential cross-section ratios relative to the total cross-section were determined, specifically for the fractions of events containing b-jets or no b-jets. These ratios were found to be 0.522 ± 0.025 (statistical) ± 0.013 (systematic) for the cases with b-jets and 0.442 ± 0.018 (statistical) ± 0.011 (systematic) for the cases without b-jets, respectively. These ratios agree with the predictions.

We investigate the time-evolution of entanglement in a disordered, interacting spin system that can be measured to see how environmental monitoring impacts it. Specifically, we either subject the system to a global measurement via a central qubit or cavity mode, or to individual measurements via an array of detector spins. Although environmental monitoring tends to suppress entanglement in isolated systems, our results reveal a different outcome - a significant increase in entanglement occurs when the system interacts with the environment over a short time frame. This phenomenon arises from the disorder-induced spontaneous generation of pairs of highly entangled spins. Our research highlights that environmental monitoring can actually boost entanglement when the observer's scale is narrower than the region of entangled spins.

Given two real numbers not equal to one ($\alpha \neq 1$) and two positive real numbers ($\beta > 0$), the set is defined as $U(\alpha, \beta) = \left\{z \in \mathbb{U} \mid \left|1 + \frac{(1-\alpha)z + \alpha}{1+\beta z}\right| > \left|\frac{\alpha}{1+\beta z}\right|\right\}$. Recent studies on generalized Bessel functions $J_{\alpha, \gamma}^{m}(z)$ and $J_{\alpha, \nu}^{m}(p)$ have motivated the current paper to investigate the properties of Janowski convexity and starlikeness for these functions. Several sufficient conditions and corollaries are derived from the analysis, including those related to convexity and starlikeness within the unit disk $\mathbb{U}$. Furthermore, specific results on Janowski convexity and starlikeness are obtained for the generalized Bessel polynomial $p_n(z)$ and Hermite polynomial $H_n(z)$.

The pandemic's long-term impact on urban centers remains uncertain, particularly regarding the transformation of public life, encounters, diversity, and community resilience. In response to this knowledge gap, researchers utilized mobile phone data to track face-to-face interactions in Spain from 2020 to 2022. Their findings revealed a notable, sustained decline in encounter diversity during the pandemic's aftermath, a phenomenon linked to the observed reduction in weekly movement radii. While the pandemic's initial effect was found to vary significantly by region and demographic group, the post-pandemic period saw a uniform, lasting disruption of social interactions. Furthermore, the study discovered that the pandemic's influence persisted more strongly in regions characterized by more intense and diverse encounters prior to the health crisis.

An algorithm named FSMSN is introduced to solve the final step of the first-order system formulation of the biharmonic equation. Key characteristics of FSMSN include its algorithmic nature and low iteration count, while avoiding non-linearity. Compared to conventional methods such as Sequential Fully Implicit method, FSMSN exhibits a faster convergence rate and maintains second-order accuracy in the residual, while its efficiency is comparable to other techniques like the Alternative Minimal Least Squares algorithm and another algorithm denoted P1Q1.

A optical cavity's handedness can profoundly influence the interaction between its internal photons and the emitters coupled with it, particularly when those emitters possess distinct chirality. This study explores how a optical cavity's orientation of a dielectric mirror can either hinder or facilitate interactions between light and specific chiral emitters. The cavity's chirality can be achieved naturally or through an artificial setup. Theemitters' interactions with light are evaluated using two primary indicators: the modification of their spontaneous emission and the transfer of their optical angular momentum to theemitters. The results reveal that the cavity's properties can be optimized to either enhance or completely block interactions between its emitters and light. The study's findings, illustrated with examples of chiral emitters of different nature, illustrate the potential of this approach to significantly boost the efficiency of optical interactions involving objects of sub-wavelength size.

Two-dimensional anti de-Sitter space is a fundamental component in various theories, including the two-dimensional string theory's semiclassical limit and the 1+1 dimensional black hole model inherent in the Jackiw Teitelboim theory. Within the Jackiw Teitelboim model, we apply the dual Riemann surface technique from large-N two-dimensional string theory to reveal the theory's underlying structure. Employing this approach offers an alternative framework that facilitates an uncomplicated determination of the partition function. Furthermore, incorporating ghosts yields modified results, including a shift in the cosmological constant and spectral shift in the theory.

Our investigation involves a fundamental quantum version of the Alcubierre warp drive, a theoretical concept proposing a method of space travel faster than light. This research explores warping solutions to the Schrodinger equation, a fundamental equation describing quantum behavior. Our findings suggest that either a novel form of negative kinetic energy or an atypical arrangement of dark energy would be necessary to achieve stable solutions in the Alcubierre warp drive framework. Additionally, certain warping solutions to the Schrodinger equation exhibit time-evolving patterns. These patterns imply a theoretical possibility of using quantum systems to detect the Alcubierre warp drive field, thereby offering a new approach to detecting this form of space warp.

The underground urban landscape houses vital infrastructure, supporting essential services such as water supply, power, and transportation. As these systems age, maintaining their optimal functioning becomes increasingly complex, necessitating proactive decision-making. We introduce a 'GUIDES' framework, which utilizes a unified, knowledge-driven approach to integrate multi-source data and assess systemic health, ultimately providing a data-driven basis for informed utility management decisions. It is envisioned that GUIDES will be deployed cloud-based, ultimately fostering a collaborative community for data sharing and development.

Our analysis in tip-enhanced Raman scattering (TERS) is rooted in a quantum mechanical framework. This approach showcases that the electromagnetic and chemical mechanisms distinct from one another, allowing us to develop separate and easily understandable models for each. Our calculations, which build upon an existing model of conventional Raman scattering, involve detailed cusp-shaped distributions of classical dipole moments positioned on both the tip and sample surfaces. By applying this model, we find that both mechanisms contribute to the overall TERS signal. However, our study provides clear indications of under what specific conditions the electromagnetic or chemical effect would be the dominant signal source. Our theoretical framework is novel as it unifies the treatment of plasmonic phenomena using classical models with Raman scattering using a quantum mechanical approach. Furthermore, our source distributions provide a suitable starting point for future developments in TERS theory.

This article showcases the largest amount of Analogous Molecular Environments
(AME) examples in a single galaxy, specifically the nearby spiral galaxy
Maffei 1. AMEs appear to be extremely rare, with only the most advanced galaxies
showing notable occurrences. Identifying them requires near-infrared spectroscopy
of individual sources. A new approach was developed for AME searches, involving
targeted observations of star-forming areas. A comprehensive survey of star-forming
regions in the northern half of the galaxy was conducted using 6.5m telescopes.
A total of 12 new AME sources were discovered in the observed northern region.
It's estimated that there are at least 200 AME sources in the entire galaxy.
A search strategy is proposed that involves observing 1% of the total star-forming
areas, which should be sufficient to find all AME sources in the galaxy. Further
research in the southern half of the galaxy is expected to reveal more AME sources,
which should allow the total number to be counted accurately in the galaxy.

Using high-resolution adiabatic calorimetry, the authors have precisely measured the entropy and specific heat of ammonium sulfate near its ferroelectric phase transition at 23.4 K under zero pressure conditions. The analysis reveals the majority of entropy change can be attributed to the vibrational modes characteristic of ferroelectrics, which includes the unique tunneling ferroelectric ground double well states. The investigation further clarifies the long-standing debate on the隧穿机制 within ammonium sulfate by providing conclusive evidence against the previously proposed theory that quantum tunneling of the tunneling entity is the primary mechanism at play.

Probability-matching is a widely observed behavior in both human and animal learning that occurs despite stronger rewards being available, such as when choosing between two options. It appears to be linked to how learners process losses, specifically during the integration of negative outcomes. Our analysis provides both theoretical and computational models showing that strategies effectively incorporating negative information delay or prevent probability-matching. These strategies, which successfully achieve higher returns, are characterized by their ability to efficiently process losses, although they don't necessarily allow for complete loss processing to reach steady-state. We corroborated our findings through both simulating LMS and Q-learning agents and conducting two human experiments. Our results indicate that delayed probability-matching could be an unintended consequence of effective learning from losses in complex environments.

Quantum mechanics is particularly noteworthy for being the first theory to exhibit nonlocality and contextuality at the algorithmic level. Although these principles are often discussed separately, research has demonstrated that they can occur simultaneously within the same quantum process. This study explores how these phenomena are connected and reveals that reconfiguring data within a quantum system is akin to transforming quantum process matrices, which facilitate a transition between processes exhibiting different levels of nonlocality and contextuality. By employing an example of quantum computation, we demonstrate that data permutations can trigger a shift from a classical process to a nonlocal and contextual one, thereby offering new insights into the relationships between these principles. This understanding may lead to novel approaches in leveraging process matrices for quantum cryptography, as well as for classifying quantum computation based on their structural properties.

This research focuses on near neighbor problems, including network searching and approximate nearest neighbor data structures. A data structure is developed, taking a given graph G of n vertices into account, to store a constant approximation factor β of the shortest path distances between vertices. By investing p = O(n^(1-ε)) = poly(n) of processing time, where 0 < ε < 1 is a constant, it can quickly answer G-based distance queries between any pair of vertices (u, v), providing an approximation of at most β * (1 + ε) of the true distance d_G(u, v), at the cost of an additional (2+ε) factor in the time it takes to answer the query. For standard query times, the structure takes O(n) of space and can answer the query in O(1) time. When dealing with weighted graphs, the structure answers the query in O(1) while incurring an additional (2+ε) factor in the approximations given, provided that it takes O(n) of space. For unweighted graphs, the structure answers the query in O(1) while incurring an additional constant factor of (1+ε) of the true distance and at the cost of a further (2+ε) factor in the time it takes to answer the query. In all cases, it is possible to take the structure to be locality sensitive hash based. These results show a significant improvement of the tradeoff between the approximation factor

A novel approach called iterative Bayesian unfolding (IBU) is proposed to address the issue of quantum noise in quantum computers. By addressing the quantum noise, IBU enables the use of quantum algorithms that demand precise input states. Unlike previous methods, IBU demonstrates enhanced scalability with increasing problem size. Through numerical evaluations, IBU surpasses other noise mitigation strategies in terms of performance and scalability. To assess IBU's capabilities, current and future quantum hardware has been simulated with various levels of noise. These simulations indicate that IBU can recover original data accurately on current quantum devices when combined with realistic gate measurements, potentially achieving 99.9% accuracy. Furthermore, IBU exhibits superior performance compared to existing methods on noise simulations, achieving an improvement of at least 3 times. By utilizing quantum algorithmic noise mitigation, IBU can achieve greater accuracy with less sampling, making it an ideal choice for use on quantum computers.

When users instruct a robot through a set of predefined actions, they often struggle to provide clear directives due to their difficulty in identifying the best course of action. To mitigate this, we have developed an interactive task-learning method that aims to simplify user instruction by simplifying the task input mapping process. We assume that both the robot and user aim to achieve the same task input mapping but disagree on what actions to use. To accomplish this, the robot's objective function is shared, while its task input mapping is learned through iterative user guidance. We have developed two variations of this approach, one where the robot discloses its task input mapping and generates a new one if user instructions are incongruent, and another where the robot hides its task input mapping to encourage user discovery. Through simulation, we found that informing the robot of its task input mapping has a positive effect on user efficiency, while comparing learned task inputs to reward functions improves efficiency further. Moreover, our approach yields comparable results to state-of-the-art methods, with revealing the task input mapping having a positive impact on learning effectiveness.

Within HiTaMap, a distinct mapping approach is developed to efficiently solve navigation problems by simplifying high-dimensional state representations. The core data structure, a HiTMap, serves as an hash-based abstract planner that stores a set of keypoint positions paired with their respective global coordinates. Navigation tasks are executed using two steps: first, the target area is localized within a specific keypoint bracket, and then a local motion planning algorithm is applied to generate an optimized path. Additionally, the HiTaMap method reduces the computational burden by limiting the integration of partial odometry, velocity, and depth data to the current keypoint bracket, thereby enabling efficient keypoint expansion.

In this research, we introduce a method to generate a class of Z-complementary array codes, termed ZCACS, for n-dimensional spaces, 2D-ZCACS for 2D arrays, utilizing a novel novel Boolean-like function. This sets apart our proposed function from established generalized Boolean functions used by Li et al. in 2015 and Chen in 2020. Based on our proposed method, we prove the capability to generate both single and multiple ZCACS, as well as 2D-ZCACS, all correlated with lower side-lobes, thus showcasing our proposed method's superiority over existing construction methods.

Reconstructing images from computed tomography scans is essential, but obtaining clear and detailed images is often a complex challenge, particularly when different forms of randomness, including differential noise and anisotropic diffusion, are present. The relationships between these noise types can be used to create a more efficient image reconstruction model. Our approach employs a novel CT image reconstruction method, designed to leverage noisy scan data and produce high-quality images, resistant to various noise contaminations. Through our approach, high-quality images can be obtained by combining noisy CT scans taken under varying diffusion conditions, and this method can be applied to other imaging tasks, providing a robust solution to complex inverse problems.

Determining the boundary where diffuse light becomes highly directional is a crucial problem in predicting how light interacts with rough surfaces, which holds significant implications for understanding planetary bodies, celestial objects, and stellar phenomena. To tackle this issue, a new method is introduced that addresses the discrepancy between complex realistic models, often requiring extensive computation, and simplified local models, which can yield inaccurate results. By comparing radiative transfer equations to their local counterparts, a revised approach determines a modified gap width, enabling a more precise description of light transport through rough surfaces, ultimately allowing for a better prediction of forward-scattered and back-scattered light. As a demonstration of its effectiveness, a particular type of rough surface, featuring exponential height fluctuations, is analyzed using this new method. To validate its accuracy, this approach is then applied to modeling the back-scattered light observed on a planetary satellite, Phobos, during sunrise and sunset.

To effectively utilize user feedback in human-AI collaboration for problem-solving, it's crucial to understand how the human contributor impacts the system. By incorporating entity retrieval with free text, we can utilize the retriever's results as context to gather human contributor feedback and refine the process. Our study, which was a blind experiment, first evaluated how well state-of-the-art retrievers could locate relevant entities out of thousands, using contributions from human participants to support a knowledge-engineering task. The results indicated that human contributor influence was a crucial factor in entity selection, with two proposed influence metrics demonstrating strong correlations with human-contributor-based evaluation, while also outperforming previous work that used the Jensen-Shannon divergence and the Gini coefficient. The blind experiment further revealed that human contributors provided unreliable answers, emphasizing the need for effective entity retrieval systems to minimize user effort. Ultimately, the study found that user impact on the retrieval system is most pronounced when near the top of the relevant results list.

Point plots, line plots, scatter plots, and their combinations are commonly used in visualizing time-based data across various fields. However, achieving seamless integration of time plots within a larger visual ecosystem can be challenging. This difficulty primarily stems from the difficulty in linking observations and the varying complexities of time series data. To overcome these issues, a new interactive technique called temporal plotting with linked views (TPWLV) is introduced in this research. This technique allows users to effectively connect time-based data with spatial data, bar charts, pie diagrams, maps, and more. It incorporates interactive techniques such as zooming, panning, and cross-filtering to enhance data comparison in a visualized environment. The proposed approach exemplifies the capabilities of modern interactive data analysis and emphasizes the importance of interconnectivity in data visualization systems.

To utilize Electronic Health Records (EHR) for graph machine learning, researchers need to develop Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks (HGNNs) to process this data type. However, existing EHRs have limitations, which pose significant obstacles to accurately predicting disease progression. To overcome these challenges, we have developed a multi-stage approach centered around generating a comprehensive disease progression graph from EHR data, which incorporates medical tests and drug prescriptions. Our approach comprises three key stages: (1) developing an HGNN architecture to extract hierarchical disease representations, (2) applying the soft attention mechanism within Heterogeneous Graph Attention Networks (HGATNs) to automatically focus on the most relevant medical tests, and (3) employing model ensemble with the proposed method to reduce over-reliance on specific tests and mitigate adverse drug effects. Our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on the evaluation benchmark created using the MIMIC-III database.

The behavior of charged soft biological materials, such as cell membranes, has been examined from the perspective of soft matter physics. These materials are characterized by their small size, high charge density, and, in many cases, small ion sizes. However, when considering larger ions, such as those found in biological contexts, a more comprehensive understanding is necessary. Using the Poisson-Boltzmann equation, this study investigates the impact of large ion size on properties near a flexible, negatively charged surface. The researchers found that as ion size increases, the ions tend to exclude themselves from the surface, resulting in a screening ion cloud. Notably, similar to electrolytes with monovalent counterions, these materials exhibit overcharging and the formation of multiple salt bridges. When ion size is increased, these materials display unique properties, such as charge reversal and the presence of multiple minima in electrostatic potential and ion density, resulting in larger ion accumulation near the surface compared to smaller ions. These findings indicate the potential for new functionality in large-ion electrolytes within soft materials.

Automated identification of software requirements from diverse sources is a crucial task.
Current methods that claim to address this problem typically involve either
hard-coded rules or black-box machine learning models with limited interpretability.
In this study, we investigated the use of BERT, a state-of-the-art,
sequence-encoded pre-trained model for NLP, on identifying software requirements.
The experimental setup was based on information retrieval and evaluated bERT's
performance against prominent models, such as fastText and ELMo, on benchmark datasets.
The bERT achieved superior results, outperforming the state-of-the-art on these datasets.
To enhance interpretability, we combined class activation maps with bERT's output,
yielding excellent identification outcomes and improved explanations of the predictions.

This research investigates the issue of minimizing energy usage in a wireless communication system where multiple users and multiple relays coexist, with users transmitting data through relays to the destination in power-limited scenarios. The study is divided into two stages, initially focusing on relay scheduling and power allocation, followed by relay beamforming at the second stage. The first stage is formulated as a mixed-integer convex optimization problem, which is resolved despite its non-convex constraints by introducing a substitution method. The non-convex quadratic power allocation problem is then transformed into a power allocation problem with linear constraints for minimization. The non-convex relay scheduling problem is solved using a bisection algorithm with improved efficiency through power adaptation and substitution methods in the final stage to find the best relay scheduling pattern. The study confirms the feasibility of finding the optimal solution by analyzing these techniques and validating their effectiveness through numerical results.

Within the mean-field approximation of the Kondo lattice model, we study the local moment states induced by superconductivity in the s-wave regime, particularly in the influence of magnetic impurities or large-scale magnetic fields. We discover that the spatial shift of the Yeshiba-Zawadzki-Shraiber (YSZ) state arises from the influence of the impurity's exchange coupling and the superconducting gap's phase gradient, as seen through an impurity's or magnetic field's impact. Additionally, we find that the spin-orbit coupling only affects the YSZ state when influenced by magnetic adatoms or dimers. Furthermore, the spin-orbit-based energy splitting becomes significant when one of the YSZ state's peaks is substantially suppressed, as seen through the impact of magnetic adatoms. This enables the use of impurity magnetism to fine-tune the superconducting spin-orbit coupling of the substrate and manipulate the YSZ state energy splitting in the case of magnetic dimers, potentially facilitating quantum information storage through the use of spin-orbit qubits.

This paper proposes a novel point cloud registration technique that takes advantage of down-sampling LIDAR point clouds to mitigate errors caused by moving objects and improve alignment accuracy. By using the structural information within point clouds for down-sampling, the technique identifies the most significant features for registration and eliminates dynamic elements that hinder the process. A real-world dataset demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method and its superiority over conventional point cloud registration algorithms.

The growing availability of extremely high-resolution satellite images, often requiring specialized knowledge for analysis, has made them an ideal resource for testing the capabilities of deep learning techniques. However, the task of using deep learning methods to process these large volumes of images is challenging due to their high memory demands. While existing solutions involve a two-stage process, they have significant limitations, particularly in terms of extended training times and decreased model accuracy. This research introduces an alternative algorithm, ALADIN, specifically designed to handle high-resolution satellite images with 16 bands, avoiding the limitations found in current methods. The proposed algorithm demonstrates comparable performance to state-of-the-art models with significantly reduced training times, even outperforming compact models in several evaluation metrics.

Using time-resolved Scanning Tunneling Microscopy, researchers investigated non-linear light interactions in metallic nickel by comparing ultrafast  and nanosecond laser pulses. This comparison revealed that when intense enough, metallic nickel experiences a shift in electron configuration leading to altered non-linear light absorption. This phenomenon occurs at high light fluences exceeding approximately 0.2 J/cm^2, enabling different electron distribution states that modify the material's light interaction properties.

This research highlights the importance of safeguarding Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based systems against increasingly sophisticated attacks. It introduces a novel approach, leveraging generative adversative networks (GANs) to simulate potential adversarial examples, and employs a two-fold objective: to generate realistic data and to anticipate adversarial threats. Through our experiments, we demonstrate that our method effectively shields DNN systems from various types of attacks across multiple domains. Notably, our simulations reveal that implementing this technique can enhance model resilience, and our future research aims to integrate this method into dynamic systems to boost their adaptive learning capabilities.

We've developed an innovative deep learning approach, based on a U-Net architecture with convolutional blocks and grouped attention mechanisms, to detect multiple sclerosis lesions in various hospital datasets. By training on one hospital's data using experience replay and then applying it to another, our method achieves excellent lesion detection across different institutions without overfitting. Furthermore, we enhanced training efficiency and model performance by incorporating multilabel batch augmentation. Our approach demonstrates state-of-the-art multiple MS lesion detection in one dataset, matches performance in another, and significantly improves lesion detection when using data from various hospitals.
A novel metric for comparing metrics on R^n is introduced, which facilitates the continuity of optimal transport. This process relies on the new metric's convergence.

In data-driven modeling, leveraging high-quality domain expertise alongside large datasets proves to be a valuable asset. We investigate the relative benefits of integrating imperfect domain knowledge versus relying solely on data-driven approaches. Our proposed method combines large-scale machine learning with a sophisticated, keyhole perspective, where a few high-dimensional features are visible. The system domain knowledge is represented as a nonlinear transformation of the observed features. Our numerical experiments indicate that the hybrid model's ability to handle imperfect domain knowledge results in (1) more efficient usage of limited data, (2) increased resilience to noisy or inaccurate domain expertise, (3) enhanced interpretability of the trained models.

Massive star formation, exemplified by objects like Rho Ophiurium-MM3, involves 
significant mass growth through the accretion of molecular cores onto the protostar. 
Our study utilizes ALMA and GCN data to examine molecular core characteristics 
at a critical stage of massive star formation. By analyzing a set of lines and 
utilizing 3D simulations, we mapped velocity fields and derived kinematic 
models to calculate the molecular core's total mass and key parameters. 
A detailed examination of molecular core morphology, velocity fields, and 
 dynamics is presented for the massive star-forming region L1551-NMW. 
Our 3D simulations suggest that a wind from the protostar ejects material in 
two jets, likely influencing the molecular core's motion and possibly 
explaning its morphology. This study provides the first instance of using 
ALMA to determine the molecular core's kinematic structure in a massive 
star-forming region, potentially shedding light on the region's complex dynamics.

The method of microlensing can reveal information about dark matter particles, but its limitations include the necessity of extremely large datasets, which may require many years to analyze. This research employed the full catalog of OGLE-III events to investigate whether primary black holes, acting as microlensing sources, are present within the Milky Way's central region. The analysis considered the effects of subhalos on the galaxy and compared observed events with theoretical predictions from dark matter theories to establish constraints. The study found that if primary black holes exist in the galaxy, they would produce approximately ten times fewer microlensing events than those caused by stars with evolved black holes. This discrepancy suggests that if primary black holes exist in the galaxy, their influence would result in a lower number of detected events. The research also established constraints on the formation of primordial black holes in the range of $10^2-10^4 M_{\odot}$ and $10^5-10^6 M_{\odot}$ and utilized the OGLE dataset to infer dark matter hypotheses based on clustering in the Milky Way's central region. The constraints were then further refined by combining OGLE data with data from the Gaia R2 source counts.

We establish a rigorous set of conditions for pantograph arrays of hard particles to reach equilibrium, uncovering two previously unknown frustrated crystal structures that form at high packing densities. An efficient algorithm is developed to identify all potential pantograph arrangements, allowing us to identify novel, stable crystal formations. A simulation of a 2D model with constrained sliding elements reveals an optimal pantograph design with packing density of 0.528 and shear-stress resistance of up to 0.028. This design is more efficient than existing alternatives, with a simulation of a 3D model yielding an even better stress-free performance of 0.014.

Pretrained language models and their associated tokenization strategies have garnered significant attention recently, particularly in recent conferences such as ACL 2021 where research on token insertion, like the newline token, has been prominent. Research studies have so far predominantly utilized existing token sets from established NLP frameworks such as BERT, without exploring the impact of adding special tokens in novel wordpiece token sets. Our work delves further into the effects of special tokens by examining the performance enhancements when inserting tokens like newline into models with fresh token sets derived from extensive text corpora. Our experimental findings reveal that newline tokens are detrimental to the performance of models trained on large text collections, contrasting with the performance boost observed in models trained on curated datasets. To understand why this occurs, we have developed theoretical frameworks and conducted additional tests to validate our hypothesis, suggesting that newline tokens contribute negatively to the token set vocabulary and promote simplifying simplifications during vocabulary construction.

We examine how to utilize real-valued network scores in the context of set function optimization, which is difficult due to the combinatorial nature of the objective function. By evaluating existing set evaluation methods in conjunction with network-assisted optimization techniques, we conduct a experiment involving image segmentation to discover that including network scores for individual pixels yields superior performance. Furthermore, we find that an adapted implementation of the Convex-Hull Cutting Plane approach outperforms the standard version in set with addition model optimizations, achieving both faster and more efficient results. Based on these findings, we propose an alternative set optimization technique that utilizes pixel-level network scores, and demonstrate that it can outperform current technique using an associated convex function.

Many glass-forming liquids exhibit thermodynamic scaling in the dynamic properties. This concept suggests a relationship between thermodynamic properties and universal behavior in these materials. Although not universally applicable, researchers believe that thermodynamic scaling reflects a relationship among properties of a glass-forming liquid, potentially indicating a glass transition point. To investigate the validity of thermodynamic scaling near a glass transition, we analyzed the scaling behavior of relaxation times in three model liquids - a polymer, a mixture of liquids, and a liquid with added nanoparticles. Our findings reveal that while thermodynamic scaling accurately describes universal behavior for two systems, it inaccurately predicts such behavior for all systems, instead suggesting distinct scaling exponents for all systems. Furthermore, our results do not support the existence of thermodynamic scaling as a reliable indicator of glass transition, suggesting the current interpretation of this scaling exponent as such may be unjustified.

Transformer-based language models excel at understanding negation in sentence pairs, 
outperforming on inference tasks that rely heavily on negative indicators.
Our study investigates the effect of removing these negative indicators from 
datasets like SQuAD, DRAGON, DragoNLI, and RACE.
Results show that models can still make accurate predictions without relying heavily 
on context to identify negation, suggesting languages using negation markers may 
not necessarily indicate advanced negation understanding capabilities.
This raises questions about the use of datasets containing negative indicators 
for tasks involving understanding negative expressions.

In the context of neural machine translation, specifically for handling extremely long source sentences, current solutions typically involve either incorporating domain-specific knowledge or employing architecture changes. Conversely, we propose an general-purpose enhancement to the Transformer model – the look-ahead attention mechanism – which enables translation systems to anticipate upcoming source sentences. Through weighted attention, the model selectively prioritizes source sentences, thus facilitating long-distance attention. Our approach requires no extra training data and shouldn't be restricted to specific translation tasks. Empirical evaluations on our most challenging English-to-German development set, using challenging sentence pairs sourced from code and social media, demonstrate significant improvements over both updated and traditional Transformer models.

In a study by N. Sibony and C. Zaidenberg on flexible symplectic scissor surgery, a specific case of symplectic cutting, flexible symplectic cotangent bundle construction is found to be equivalent to the more general concept for any symplectic manifold. This general concept, when further simplified, allows the expression of curvature weights in terms of exact 1-forms rather than closed 1-forms. This discovery resolves a problem posed by S. Boyallian and provides a global framework for the work on flexible Scanning developed by C. Gaspar and on dynamical scanning by S. Gaspar and C. Zaidenberg.

Our research explores the behavior of higher spin currents in three-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) by focusing on their thermal entropy and dispersion relations, ultimately relating this to the R-symmetry current's properties through properties of higher spin CFTs. We also investigate the dual gauge theory behavior in terms of the mass deformation of a U(1) gauge theory with charged spin particles. The findings reveal a novel connection between the higher spin currents and the gauge theory behavior, specifically the mass gap and Debye mass. We further discover a significant difference in the behavior of thermal entropy across dimensions. For three-dimensional CFTs, the properties are either unsaturated or saturated and increase with the coupling, whereas in four-dimensional CFTs, the properties exhibit saturation regardless of the coupling strength.

We offer a straightforward method for pricing Asian options using single asset models with Laplace-transformed prices. This method allows us to apply it to various scenarios, including continuous Asian options on stocks, Asian options on stocks with dividends, Asian options on stocks with a convenience yield and floating rate Asian options. Furthermore, we extend our approach to price Asian options with barriers and derive new constant maturity formulas for looking-back put options. Our method also yields analytical solutions for pricing Asian options with barriers.

Recent research suggests that galaxy clusters form the primary contribution to the observed diffuse gamma-ray background. However, previous studies predicting gamma-ray emissions from these clusters were not sufficient to account for their observed contribution. Predictions were based on the assumption that the high-energy gamma-rays were produced solely through the interaction of high-energy protons with the baryonic matter in the clusters. This study presents gamma-ray emission maps from 14 clusters based on a comprehensive X-ray survey. Previous to this study's findings, no significant gamma-ray emissions were detected from 11 of these 14 clusters. Nevertheless, when combining the measured and predicted fluxes from all 14 clusters, the resulting diffuse gamma-ray background could account for a considerable portion of the observed diffuse gamma-ray flux. This study's findings challenge the conventional understanding that thermal plasma within clusters is the primary component of high-energy gamma-ray emissions. Furthermore, this study's findings suggest that galaxy clusters may form the primary anisotropic component of the observed gamma-ray background.

Inflationary models with enhanced non-Gaussianities hold promise for accurately forecasting the primordial universe. This is particularly true for models featuring abrupt changes in primordial behavior, which often leave distinct, visually distinct marks in primordial non-Gaussianity, with characteristic scales that can be recognized throughout observable history. These "pleasing non-Gaussian models" can be further analyzed, with specific examples, including multi-field inflation models, demonstrating how complex features can be represented in simpler single-field models, often resulting in consistent observational data. A further example has been discovered in single-field models, with a distinctive plateau on the potential's second derivative, yielding a non-Gaussian model with unique characteristics. These examples provide a broad range of perspectives, with predictions that are often consistent across theories, with the possibility that these observations may be used to accurately describe future findings.

Deep learning models have significantly advanced numerous fields, but their decision-making process remains difficult to grasp, making it challenging to assess their accuracy and potential risks. We propose the Latent Visual Semantic Explainer (LaViSE), an innovative approach that uses dynamic visualization techniques to illustrate text descriptions about its underlying representation, leveraging large language models to automatically generate explanations. LaViSE's text representations are automatically refined and translated back into natural language, allowing us to effectively assess our method on a broad range of tasks without requiring task-specific parameters. The results show that our approach effectively identifies the most relevant areas in images, particularly in complex scenarios, without requiring advanced settings or external guidance. Furthermore, we have developed a novel assessment method for text generation that doesn't rely on existing benchmarks, along with a new assessment dataset for representing complex image features. The code for LaViSE is available on GitHub at https://github.com/ashwinkumar21/LaViSE.

The diverse structural, chemical, and physical characteristics of high-temperature superconductors pose challenges for high-temperature superconductivity research. Our machine learning-driven analysis reveals that structural similarities in 2D cuprates are predictable based on their 1D counterparts. This discovery provides a framework for exploring the physical properties of 2D cuprates through their 1D analogs, a concept supported by machine learning findings.

HIV care access is heavily reliant on accurate treatment opportunity identification. However, individuals' awareness of their travel time to care is often uncertain. Traditional studies have relied on self-reported data, but neglecting the variability of estimated times. Our study analyzed over 100,000 individuals across 27 countries, focusing on the relationship between average and maximum travel times to HIV care and potential treatment rates. Utilizing unique country-level metrics for familiarity, we discovered significant correlations between average travel times and treatment occurrence. Our findings suggest that individuals more likely to utilize care are those with reduced travel times, but increased familiarity with longer travel times can also lead to higher treatment rates. Our research highlights the importance of considering both average and maximum travel times to HIV care.

The study of vortex lattices in thin, thin films of two types of ferromagnets, and their transition to stable states under negative magnetic field influence, has been studied. In this investigation, we have examined the effect of magnetic field influence on the metastable state of thin films, and further explored the transition of this lattice to a 'cone phase' in sub-saturation fields. Through analysis of the energy of the system, we have discovered that a transition occurs when the size of the vortex core is approximately half that of the lattice period. The study utilized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau model to analyze the dynamic behavior of the system and its change from the metastable skyrmion lattice to the cone phase. The investigation revealed two distinct mechanisms causing the transition, and demonstrated one of these mechanisms, where skyrmions shrink until they disappear at specific field intensities. The remaining ferromagnetic background then undergoes twisting motion to reach a cone state. The time required for this transition was also studied and revealed a characteristic time constant of approximately 100 picoseconds for the transition process.

This article examines the connection between singular ARMA models and high-dimensional dynamic factor models for series with mixed ARMA representations, offering both theoretical insights and practical applications. A notable outcome of our work shows that singular ARMA models are crucial for constructing HD-DFM models, as they provide the framework for the joint time series behavior of high-dimensional factor loadings, thereby enabling new possibilities in time series factor analysis. The results are applied to several financial factor models, demonstrating the effectiveness of incorporating singular ARMA models in analyzing both common factors and factor-specific idiosyncratic components.

Let $K$ be a closed convex subset of a Hilbert space and let $F$ be a monotone mapping from the set $K$ to the negative cone of $K$. The paper explores the equilibrium problem under these conditions and introduces the proximal point algorithm for finding solutions. A key finding is that the equilibrium points of the more recent mapping are the solutions to the original problem, under the assumption that the step size is sufficiently small. The algorithm is then demonstrated to converge strongly in certain situations. The concept of y-coercivity is also used in analyzing these findings.

Deep learning models are widely used for their impressive performance, but their limitations are often unclear. The issue is compounded by the absence of a theoretical framework to analyze deep neural networks. Conversely, Bayesian methods can place uncertainty quantification at the center of their focus, but their application to deep neural networks is hindered by the computational demands. To bridge this gap, a novel Bayesian approach called Bayesian by shallow contextualization (BBSC) is proposed. BBSC achieves uncertainty quantification efficiently by employing contextual embeddings and employing Bayesian techniques at a lower level. Empirical evidence demonstrates that BBSC can provide well-calibrated predictions for complex tasks such as image classification on the ImageNet dataset, as well as for advanced language modeling on the GPT-2 model. The underlying theory of BBSC is grounded in Bayesian inference within the context of deep neural networks, with predictive performance evaluated based on marginal likelihood.

A long-standing goal in solar and astrophysics is to develop a comprehensive model of a dynamo that accurately replicates the dynamic behavior of solar and stellar magnetic fields. Achieving this goal, however, poses significant challenges due to the complex and turbulent nature of these processes. High-resolution simulations indicate that all forms of turbulence must be accounted for in modeling dynamos, requiring a comprehensive approach rather than relying on simplified approximations. Despite this, many previous studies have employed a combination of magnetohydrodynamic and alpha-effect dynamo theories to describe gyrodynes. Our study aims to demonstrate the critical importance of accounting for all turbulent effects in early solar cycle simulations and the dynamo operating depth in age-cooler stars. Furthermore, our findings suggest that the magnetic cycle's period and amplitude are highly sensitive to the accounting for all turbulent effects, particularly within convective layers containing thin convective cells.

A comprehensive study of outflows in the nucleus of the galaxy NGC4945 has been conducted using a large dataset from the ATLAS2F survey. This research utilized the IRAM NOEMA telescope to observe CO and CO-based molecular outflow in the region, while the MOCASSIN survey's SiO data allowed the derivation of outflow kinematics and morphologies from a single side lobe. Simultaneously, NOEMA's sensitive data enabled detection of the highly supersonic molecular outflow extending in the opposite direction, which was not seen in the other LoB's SiO data. Combining these observations with radio recombination line data, the study constrained the mass outflow to approximately 1.6x10^7 Mo within 1.5x10^3 pc and the mechanical power of the outflow was estimated to be approximately 1.2x10^39 erg/s. This study confirms the role of the large starburst in driving gas outflows and the role of the active galactic nucleus in driving outflows is difficult to determine, given the calculated mechanical power of the outflow is lower than the energy input from both the starburst and the active galactic nucleus.

A novel approach has been developed for simulating the growth of broadband spectral energies in beam-plasma instabilities within the framework of the Fokker-Planck formalism. This methodology is rooted in a novel interpretation of the quasilinear theory which establishes a connection between the growth rates of the wave spectral energy density and the particle probability density function, rather than the traditionally employed distribution functions described by Maxwell, delta, Maschke or Weibel distributions. Simulation results reveal that particle distributions resembling the Maxwell or Maschkeze distributions become established when broad-band spectral energies grow with equal QGPs among a limited number of particles. Conversely, when spectral energies increase with the same QGP for a large number of particles, the particle distribution resembles either the Maschke or Weibel distributions. Furthermore, the required time-step in these simulations is directly proportional to the inverse of the highest-frequency instability, making them computationally efficient even for the rapid QGP associated with the Weibel instability.

Over the past few years, spectral element methods with linear basis functions have gained popularity due to their ease of implementation and computational efficiency. On the other hand, methods utilizing higher-degree polynomial bases have shown great promise in numerical simulations, particularly in problems requiring high resolution. Our study introduces two new variable-step-size variants of the spectral element method using linear elements for unstructured grid implementations. The variable stepsizes enable more accurate representation of complex physical features on non-uniform grids. The proposed methods are demonstrated using various uniform and non-uniform grid configurations in a heat conduction problem. The results indicate that the accuracy of the uniform-grid-based method is comparable to that of its non-uniform-grid-based counterpart.

This research investigates the connections between key properties of linear differential inclusions, including exponential boundedness, observability, and left invertibility, with resolvent properties and solutions to the Lyapunov inequality. We establish that specific property combinations can be characterized by a generalized Lyapunov inequality, which encompasses both generalized observability and left invertibility. We define generalized observability and left invertibility in terms of solutions to the Lyapunov inequality and demonstrate that they serve as equivalent conditions for the boundedness of the C₀-semigroup and its unique weak* continuous limit.

A code called MuMuPy has been created to facilitate estimation of the probabilities key to the search for the rare $B_s\rightarrow\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+μ^-$ transition and to determine the properties of dimuonium. The results in the form of binding energy, radius, and relative velocity of dimuonium can then be used by theoretical models to calculate new standard model predictions for $b\to s$ decays when dimuonium is present.

We examine how relative wealth and absolute wealth interrelate in a unified framework through a uniquely defined utility function and utilize it to solve a investment portfolio optimization problem. By considering discrete time steps and continuous time periods, and using the Black-Scholes model along with a specific risk aversion criterion, our framework allows for the analytically determined optimal portfolio returns. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that no conflict exists between pursuing absolute and relative gains when outcomes are guaranteed.

Recent discoveries of young star-forming galaxies outside of dense clusters have led to intriguing questions about the properties and evolution of local galaxies, particularly in relation to the early Universe. To investigate this issue, we conducted a comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of 13 highly star-forming local galaxies, known as Green Pea galaxies, using a large APOGEE dataset. Our data reveal that these galaxies, characterized by their young ages, intense star formation rates, and low dust content, share several similarities with the early Universe, including the presence of strong emission lines, low metallicities, and sub-solar oxygen-to-helium abundance ratios. Furthermore, our findings suggest that the star formation histories of Green Pea galaxies are short-lived, with their star formation rates likely to have been significantly higher in the past. Moreover, the spectral energy distributions of Green Pea galaxies are well-matched by models assuming unobstructed starlight, whereas other galaxies typically exhibit significant obscuration. Ultimately, our research implies that the properties of Green Pea galaxies may have once been universal, with the effect of internal feedback likely playing a crucial role in the rapid transformation and eventual departure from this state for a significant fraction of star-forming galaxies, likely during the early epochs following galaxy formation.

Researchers have utilized a specialized quantum simulator to investigate the behavior of a novel model involving a fermion and a boson with a spin-dependent interaction that varies periodically. This model's emergence in a Hamiltonian framework reveals its application in both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic materials. The model's complex dynamics, characterized by the interplay of spin rotation and the non-trivial behavior of the boson, results in unique aspects of the fermion's energy spectrum, namely the rotation of its polarization axis and a phenomenon analogous to Zeno effects that restricts the boson's movement under continuous rotation.

We've discovered that the braided Thompson's groups $B$ and $B^+$ have a characteristic with linear divergence. To reach this conclusion, we developed a group metric that preserves conjugacy, and then used it to quantify the divergence of an element in. This approach ultimately set the foundation for identifying the maximally divergent element in $B_2$.

This paper examines the problem of customizing Retrieval Augmented Generation systems, which combines language models and search engines to produce accurate and up-to-date responses based on both learned knowledge and contextual relevance. This customization involves both adjusting the generation model's parameters and optimizing vector space embeddings to enhance retrieval processes. This study investigates the complexities of adapting RAG architecture and assesses state-of-the-art techniques for both optimization components. Furthermore, a minimal framework has been developed to standardize RAG fine-tuning, which we hope will unify the various approaches and accelerate future research in this field.

Through Riemann-Hilbert methods, we establish precise asymptotic information for two precise models: one being the high-energy eigenfunction sign oscillation pattern for the harmonic oscillator, and another a model representing random matrix and Fermi gas correlations, specifically the Fermi gas model proposed by Logan and Van den Berg. In both scenarios, Riemann-Hilbert methods transform the problem into a simpler scenario on a transformed domain with simplified behavior, allowing us to derive precise asymptotics. Notably, this second model has been recently analyzed using another Riemann-Hilbert model proposed by Deift, Chihara and McLaughlin.

Recent studies have demonstrated the potential for human learning from AI-generated output. Nevertheless, most existing models are assessed by high-quality annotations, which are laborious and costly to create. To expedite the annotation process, this study investigates how to leverage low-quality, self-qualified annotations for automatic summarization. We develop a straightforward pipeline to identify high-quality annotations and establish a QualQual benchmark containing 4,000 qualifications. This benchmark includes 100 samples for evaluation, 100 as reference, 1,900 as reference, 2,000 as reference, and 1,000 as reference. 

By focusing on qualified annotations, the proposed method yields significant improvements in F1 score and other metrics, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods by up to 4.5% and significantly enhancing the model's performance in the domain. 

To further enhance the model's performance, we develop an annotation qualification module (AQMod) that selects optimal qualified annotations for training the model. The combination of the QualQual dataset and the AQMod yields state-of-the-art performance in automatic summarization.

The effectiveness of large video models for text and video retrieval is significantly constrained by their limited ability to capture intricate details in spatiotemporal video content. In this study, we introduce TS2-Net, a novel architecture that enhances the quality of video representations by combining advanced noise and content-based distortion estimations during training.
